title: Split Array Largest Sum
summary: Cut an array into k contiguous pieces so that the largest piece sum is as small as possible.

tests.explain: Cutting after the 3 gives [6, 3] and [8, 2, 5], with sums 9 and 15. The other cuts give a largest sum of 18, 17 or 19, so 15 is the best.
Cut in the middle: [4, 4] and [4, 4], both summing to 8. Any other cut leaves one piece with at least 12.
With k equal to the length, every element is its own piece, so the largest piece is the largest element.

hints: Turn the question around: given a limit L, can you cut the array into at most k pieces whose sums are all <= L?
That check is greedy: walk left to right and start a new piece only when adding the next number would exceed L. If L works, every bigger limit works too.
So binary search on L between max(nums) (no piece can be smaller than the biggest element) and sum(nums) (one piece). Find the first L whose greedy piece count is <= k.

complexity.time: O(n log S): log S candidate limits, where S is the total sum, each checked in O(n)
